central_question: What really is the good news in our context?

variants.title: Church
variants.status: Recovered baseline; wording lightly edited for clarity

blocks.title: Target Audience
questions: Who is our most important target audience? Which sub-groups exist?
What role do faith and spirituality play in their lives?
What alternatives do people already use for the needs, values and interests that connect us?

blocks.title: Connecting Factor
questions: What are the three most important connecting factors: problems, values, needs or interests?
Which interest-based activities align with our ministry’s values and people’s interests?
Which existing relationships or networks can help us connect?

blocks.title: Missional Identity
questions: What really is the good news in our context?
How does our church reflect God’s mission in the world?
What aspects of our ministry are particularly compelling to people in this context?

blocks.title: Relationships
questions: What type of relationship do people expect from us: community, co-creation, accountability, self-service or another form?
How can our relational offerings be accessible and welcoming to people new to faith?

blocks.title: Key Activities
questions: Which activities are required to connect with and serve people effectively?
Which activities sustain this work over time: worship, communication, events or training?

blocks.title: Channels
questions: Where and how will we meet the people we are called to serve?
Which relationships already exist, and which need to be established with people, the city and partner organizations?

blocks.title: Resources
questions: What do we need: finances, volunteers, staff, partnerships, equipment, technology, materials and space?

blocks.title: Budget
questions: What are the costs: rent, salaries, utilities, communication, technology and materials?

blocks.title: Assessing Missional Effectiveness
questions: How will we cultivate prayerful discernment and openness to the Holy Spirit as we assess our church’s missional effectiveness?
Which SMART criteria align with our God-given mission and help us understand impact and areas for growth?

blocks.title: Target Audience
questions: Whom are we called to serve, and who is affected by our work?
How do people describe their own hopes, needs, faith and context?
Who is absent from our current understanding?

blocks.title: Connecting Factor
questions: Where do our calling and people’s lived needs meet?
Which local strengths, interests and trusted relationships can we build on?
What support already exists, and where should we partner?

blocks.title: Missional Identity
questions: What really is the good news in our context?
How does our work participate in God’s mission through the hope of Jesus Christ, service, justice and reconciliation?
How will this take a concrete form that people recognize as good—not merely our intention?

blocks.title: Relationships
questions: How will people shape the work, exercise agency and hold us accountable?
What support can someone receive without joining, donating, or participating in religious activity?
How do we build trust across differences of belief and power?

blocks.title: Key Activities
questions: Which services, advocacy or community practices make our missional identity tangible?
What must we sustain, change, partner on or stop?

blocks.title: Channels
questions: Where do people already seek help or gather?
How will trusted partners, physical presence and digital access work together?
Which barriers must we remove?

blocks.title: Resources
questions: Which people, skills, partnerships, safeguarding, space and technology does the work require?
What strengths do the communities we serve bring, and how will their contribution be recognized?

blocks.title: Budget
questions: What does this work cost, and how will grants, gifts or earned income sustain it?
What conditions do funders attach, and could they distort our mission?
How will we account transparently for resources and protect access to help?

blocks.title: Assessing Missional Effectiveness
questions: What do prayer, Scripture and the people we serve reveal about our faithfulness?
What evidence of improved lives and unintended harm will we examine alongside financial sustainability?
Who can challenge our interpretation, and what would lead us to change or stop?

blocks.title: Target Audience
questions: Who uses, pays for, produces and is affected by our product or service?
What are their lived needs and contexts, including employees, suppliers and neighbors?
Who bears costs without being represented in purchasing decisions?

blocks.title: Connecting Factor
questions: Which real needs, hopes or shared concerns connect our calling to this work?
What do people already do, and what would serve them better?
Which relationships and capabilities give us a responsible place to contribute?

blocks.title: Missional Identity
questions: What really is the good news in our context?
How does our vocation participate in God’s mission through the hope of Jesus Christ and the goods of honest work, justice, service and reconciliation?
What does that calling require of our product, employment and ownership decisions? A commercial offer cannot stand in for the gospel.

blocks.title: Relationships
questions: What should customers, employees and partners be able to expect from us?
How will we protect freedom, privacy, fair treatment and honest relationships across beliefs?
How can people question, decline or leave without pressure or penalty disguised as spiritual obligation?

blocks.title: Key Activities
questions: What must we design, make, deliver and maintain to embody this calling?
How will sourcing, employment and the product’s use express the same commitments?
Which profitable activities would we refuse or stop?

blocks.title: Channels
questions: Where and how will people encounter, obtain and receive support for our work?
How will sales and marketing tell the truth without exploiting vulnerability?
Which distribution partners reinforce or undermine our commitments?

blocks.title: Resources
questions: Which people, skills, capital, partnerships, materials and technology are entrusted to us?
How will ownership, governance and incentives protect the mission as we grow?

blocks.title: Budget
questions: What costs, wages, prices and revenue model can sustain useful work fairly?
Who carries financial risk and receives the value created?
Which revenue opportunities conflict with our calling, and how will we fund the cost of refusing them?

blocks.title: Assessing Missional Effectiveness
questions: What does faithful participation in God’s mission look like here, alongside a sustainable business?
What evidence will we examine about usefulness, work, justice, relationships and unintended harm—not only growth or profit?
How will prayerful discernment, independent challenge and changed context inform what we continue, revise or end?
